justifications.functional_suitability: Real-Time Scoring Service and Scoring Engine Component cover R-01; Case Management Backend with Workflow Engine covers R-02; Model Event Bus hot-reload plus signed artifacts partially covers R-03. Gaps: no rules engine or rule-update component, and the decline/approve/review decision path is not explicit.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Feature Store Cache Component, in-memory ONNX Scoring Engine, DynamoDB Feature Store and asynchronous Audit Event Publisher/SQS support 50 ms. Gaps: synchronous DynamoDB audit write and vault token resolution in the hot path, API Gateway plus ALB plus proxy hops, and no autoscaling or capacity plan for 3,000 TPS.
justifications.compatibility: Defined protocols per integration: gRPC from Payment Gateway / Acquirer, mTLS to Card Networks & Tokenization Vault, REST to Core-Banking / Ledger System, signed artifacts from Model Training Environment. Gaps: inconsistent HTTPS vs gRPC ingress, no ISO 8583/acquirer standard adapters, and unclear disposition flow.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analyst is served by Analyst Portal API Controller over HTTPS with MFA/RBAC and masked data via Tokenization & Masking Service Client. Gaps: no analyst UI container or explanation display, and the Payment Gateway integration is machine-only with no operator tooling.
justifications.reliability: Circuit Breaker / Fallback Component, SQS FIFO with DLQ, SNS decoupling, managed DynamoDB/RDS and Resilience4j address R-07. Gaps: fallback policy is unspecified, there is no multi-AZ or recovery design, a single region, and synchronous audit writes can fail the scoring path.
justifications.security: AWS WAF, mTLS, Go Routing & Tokenization Proxy scrubbing PANs, KMS CMK encryption, TLS 1.3, MFA/RBAC, masked analyst views, S3 Object Lock archive and signed model artifacts address R-05/R-06. Gaps: no explicit PCI segmentation, hash-chain detail, or IAM/secrets design.
justifications.maintainability: Clear container and component decomposition: Scoring Service split into handler, token client, cache, engine, dispatcher and circuit breaker; messaging decoupling; managed AWS services suit three engineers. Gaps: mixed Go and Java stacks, multiple data technologies, and ambiguous Redis versus embedded cache.
justifications.portability: Containerized Go and Java services on ECS and standard PostgreSQL help somewhat, but the design is deeply tied to AWS-specific services such as DynamoDB, SQS, EventBridge, Lambda, Signer and Glacier, with no abstraction layers. Single-region eu-west-1 matches the brief, but replaceability is limited.

sensitivity_points: Synchronous token resolution to external vault in the hot path
Two hops (gateway, Go proxy) before scoring
Audit write to DynamoDB, if synchronous
tradeoffs: In-memory ONNX scoring is fast but limits model complexity
API Gateway plus proxy adds latency versus security filtering
PERF-01.justification: In-memory scoring and feature cache suit 50 ms. But the external vault call, API Gateway+ALB+proxy hops and the synchronous audit write are unquantified latency risks; no capacity sizing for 3,000 TPS is shown.

sensitivity_points: Shared RDS load only from case workflow
Masked-data fetch from external vault per case screen
tradeoffs: Separate Fargate backend and RDS isolate analysts from scoring but add cost
PERF-02.justification: Case management runs in separate containers with its own PostgreSQL, decoupled via SQS, so analyst load barely touches scoring. Case screen 2 s depends on vault calls, with no caching shown.

sensitivity_points: Fallback component is inside the crashing service
No defined fallback decision logic or rules
No multi-AZ or autoscaling stated
tradeoffs: Fail-open keeps payments flowing but raises fraud risk
AVAIL-01.justification: The fallback sits inside the scoring service, so a crash takes it down too. There is no external fail-open path at the gateway, no health-check failover, and no audited fallback decision mechanism. Significant changes needed.

sensitivity_points: Direct synchronous DynamoDB write in decision path
No local buffer or durable spill when store is down
tradeoffs: Synchronous audit gives durability but couples latency to the store
AVAIL-02.justification: An SNS async publisher exists, and DynamoDB is highly available, but the scoring service writes directly to DynamoDB. No buffering or retry guarantees no loss, and decoupling of latency from the store is not explicit.

sensitivity_points: Hot-reload signal via EventBridge
No model registry or version store
No explicit model version in decision record
tradeoffs: In-process hot reload avoids downtime but lacks canary isolation
MOD-01.justification: EventBridge hot-reload and signed artifacts enable zero-downtime swap. But there is no model registry, rollback mechanism, canary, or stated recording of model version in decisions, leaving rollback within 5 minutes and referencing unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: No rules engine or rule store exists
Analysts have no rule authoring interface
tradeoffs: Rules embedded in model code would require redeployment
MOD-02.justification: The architecture has no rule engine, rule repository, analyst rule-authoring UI, or recording of applied rules and explanations. Only ML model artifacts are handled. Meeting this needs a new component.

sensitivity_points: Tokenized data only reaches the backend
MFA/RBAC present but no anomaly detection
Masking client talks to the vault
tradeoffs: Tokenization protects PANs but adds vault dependency and latency
SEC-01.justification: Tokenization at the edge and masking mean analysts see no PANs, and MFA/RBAC exist. However, no monitoring, such as CloudTrail/GuardDuty, or alerting within 15 minutes is defined. The masking client talking to the vault is ambiguous.

sensitivity_points: Explanation content not explicitly stored
Glacier retrieval time and no query index
DynamoDB tamper-evidence is not hash chained
tradeoffs: Glacier is cheap for 7 years but slows retrieval
SEC-02.justification: S3 Object Lock and Glacier archive give 7-year tamper-resistant retention, and retrieval fits one working day. But the explanation, inputs and model version are not explicitly in the record, no explainability component exists, and there is no lookup index.
